A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedCOF research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, and retained content can be matched across extensive renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification benchmarks, fine-tuning and linear-probing experiments, ablations, DomainNet feature-shift tests, and privacy-noise experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional optimization comparisons, linear-probing results, and a shrinkage ablation.

M1.justification: The covariance estimator, shrinkage, removal of between-class scatter, classifier normalization, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Multiple means per client and accumulation across rounds already appear in v1. Adding class counts explicitly to Table 1 clarifies information already required by v1's algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet pre-training and the same classification coverage: CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, CUB200, Cars, iNat-120K, CIFAR-10 pre-training comparisons, and six-domain DomainNet feature shift. The additional optimization experiments reuse existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: v2 adds FedAvg to the SqueezeNet fine-tuning comparison alongside FedAdam and the initialized methods (v1 Figure 6 versus v2 Figure 3 and Table 4). FedAvg previously appeared in other comparisons, but not this one. The principal training-free comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Follow-up optimization protocols are substantially revised: v2 changes SqueezeNet fine-tuning after FedCOF/Fed3R from 200 to 100 rounds, introduces a 100-round comparison table, changes Cars learning rates, and reports three local epochs for iNat linear probing instead of v1's general one-epoch specification. The Cars probing plot changes from ViT-B/16 to SqueezeNet. Some reporting remains inconsistent: Section 5.3 gives FedNCM 200 fine-tuning rounds, whereas Appendix J states 100 after initialization.

E4.justification: v2 adds a shrinkage sensitivity analysis on ImageNet-R and CUB200, testing gamma values from 0 to 10 in Table 9. Client-count, heterogeneity, multiple-mean, covariance-approximation, feature-shift, and privacy-noise analyses were already present in v1 and are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports three-seed averaging for the fine-tuning curves in Figure 3 and provides uncertainty values in Table 4; v1's corresponding Figure 6 did not specify its run count. Five-seed benchmark and privacy reporting remain unchanged. This establishes expanded reporting, not an increase in runs.

E6.justification: The follow-up optimization evidence expands substantially through new FedAvg results, revised fine-tuning curves, and iNat linear-probing trajectories after different initializations. v2 reports FedCOF-initialized probing reaching 34% within 1000 rounds, versus 27.3% after 5000 rounds for random initialization, and adds shrinkage results in Table 9. Cars ViT probing results are replaced by SqueezeNet results. The principal training-free benchmark table is numerically identical; changed settings prevent interpreting the revised optimization results as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–3, their proofs, the covariance and classifier derivations, and the non-iid bias analysis are mathematically retained. The bias analysis moves from Appendix J to E. Newly labeled proof sketches and the expanded convergence paragraph restate reasoning already present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: covariance estimation from client means, training-free classifier initialization, improved accuracy at FedNCM's communication cost, competitiveness with Fed3R, and better subsequent optimization. The additional comparisons support these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation linking shrinkage benefits to limited data and unreliable covariance estimates. It removes v1's hypotheses that pre-training makes class features more iid and that less noisy estimates explain outperforming the oracle. It also removes the explicit limitation that large domain shifts from pre-training may impair performance, while retaining the client-count and iid limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix J expands implementation information for random-initialization baselines and iNat linear probing, including method-specific learning rates, local epochs, and participation. Other settings are revised as described under E3. The FLSim framework, RTX 6000 hardware, and code URL remain the same.

R1.justification: v2 removes the cited works by Goswami et al. (2023), Magistri et al. (2024), and Papyan et al. (2020), trimming the continual-learning shrinkage and neural-collapse context. Related work is rewritten to emphasize training-free use of pre-trained models, while the central positioning relative to FedNCM and Fed3R remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the document: it introduces a dedicated training-based comparison subsection and an Impact Statement, separates additional ablations from experiments, and extensively reorders the appendices. Related-work, method, and experimental prose is condensed or rewritten, although the abstract and main scientific narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one-column to two-column layout, with extensive table, algorithm, and figure rearrangement. v1's scatter-ablation bar chart becomes v2 Table 2; communication and covariance-ablation plots move to appendices. Optimization plots receive changed axes, legends, and initialization markers, and new comparison and shrinkage tables are added.

improvement.justification: The new shrinkage sweep, additional trained-baseline comparisons, and iNat probing trajectories modestly strengthen validation of the existing method. Expanded seed and optimizer information also helps assess the experiments. These benefits are tempered by removal of the pre-training domain-shift caveat and new reporting inconsistencies, including conflicting fine-tuning budgets and a Cars plot labeled SqueezeNet while the discussion still says ViT-B/16. The core method, theory, and principal benchmark results remain unchanged.
